title: IEEE EMBC Annual Conference
organization: IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
description: The flagship annual international conference of the IEEE EMBS, bringing together researchers across biomedical engineering, health informatics, and medical devices. Students can submit papers, present posters, and attend workshops and networking events.
typicalTiming: Conference held mid-year (usually July); paper submissions typically open in the preceding winter.
eligibility: Open to students, researchers, and professionals worldwide. Reduced student registration rates available.

title: BMES Annual Meeting
description: The largest annual gathering of biomedical engineers in the United States, drawing an international audience. Features research presentations, career fairs, a design competition, and dedicated undergraduate and graduate student programming.
typicalTiming: Held annually in the autumn (October/November); abstract submissions open in the spring.
eligibility: Open to students and professionals worldwide; BMES student membership offers discounted registration.

title: DAAD RISE
description: Summer research internships in Germany placing undergraduate students from around the world with doctoral researchers in science and engineering, including biomedical and life sciences projects. Includes a stipend and support.
typicalTiming: Applications generally open in autumn/winter for the following summer placement.
eligibility: Undergraduate students in science and engineering enrolled outside Germany (RISE Germany strand); English is the working language.

title: EMBL Internships & EICAT Programme
description: Research and traineeship opportunities at EMBL sites across Europe in molecular biology, bioinformatics, imaging, and computational biology. Placements let students work in world-class laboratories and core facilities.
typicalTiming: Openings posted throughout the year; timing varies by group and programme.
eligibility: Students and early-career researchers; specific requirements vary by position and are listed on each posting.

title: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
description: Paid summer research internships in NIH laboratories across biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research. Interns work alongside leading scientists and participate in seminars, workshops, and a poster day.
typicalTiming: Applications typically open in autumn/winter for the following summer.
eligibility: Students who are US citizens or permanent residents (per program requirements) enrolled in high school, college, or graduate/professional programs.

title: Fulbright Foreign Student Program
organization: US Department of State / Fulbright Program
description: Prestigious grants enabling graduate students and researchers from over 160 countries to study, conduct research, and teach in the United States, including STEM and biomedical fields.
typicalTiming: Deadlines are set locally by each country's Fulbright Commission or US Embassy; generally the year before the study period.
eligibility: Varies by country; typically graduating seniors, graduate students, and professionals. Apply through your home country's Fulbright office.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
description: Fully funded international joint master's degrees delivered by consortia of European and partner universities, including programmes in medical imaging, biomedical engineering, and health informatics. Students study in multiple countries.
typicalTiming: Each programme sets its own application window, usually opening in autumn for the next academic year.
eligibility: Bachelor's degree holders worldwide; scholarship covers tuition, travel, and living costs for selected students.

title: Google Summer of Code
description: A global, remote program where new contributors work on open-source software projects with mentoring organizations. Many participating orgs focus on scientific computing, bioinformatics, and medical imaging tools.
typicalTiming: Organizations announced in late winter; contributor applications open in spring for a summer coding period.
eligibility: Open to individuals 18+ who are new or beginner contributors to open source; no longer limited to students.

title: iGEM Competition
description: A worldwide synthetic biology competition where student teams design and build biological systems to address real-world problems, culminating in the annual Grand Jamboree. Strong emphasis on interdisciplinary teamwork and outreach.
typicalTiming: Teams register and work over the spring and summer; the Grand Jamboree is held in the autumn.
eligibility: Student teams (high school, undergraduate, and overgraduate divisions) organized through universities and institutions worldwide.

title: MIT Hacking Medicine Hackathons
description: Health-focused hackathons that bring together engineers, clinicians, designers, and business students to rapidly prototype solutions to healthcare challenges. Events are run at MIT and with partners around the world.
typicalTiming: Multiple events across the year; dates and locations announced on the official site.
eligibility: Open to students and professionals from diverse backgrounds; individual events may have specific criteria.

title: Rice 360° Global Health Technologies Design Competition
organization: Rice University — Rice 360° Institute for Global Health Technologies
description: An annual competition showcasing student-designed technologies that address global health challenges, especially for low-resource settings. Teams present functional prototypes to judges and a public audience.
typicalTiming: Held in the spring; applications and abstracts are usually due earlier in the academic year.
eligibility: Undergraduate and graduate student teams from universities worldwide developing global health technologies.

title: HeroX Crowdsourcing Challenges
description: A crowdsourcing platform hosting incentive prize challenges, many in health, medicine, and biotechnology. Participants worldwide submit solutions to open innovation problems posed by organizations and agencies.
typicalTiming: Challenges run on rolling, independent timelines; browse active challenges anytime.
eligibility: Varies per challenge; many are open to individuals and teams internationally.

title: Kaggle Machine Learning Competitions
description: A global data science platform hosting machine learning competitions, including many medical imaging, genomics, and healthcare prediction challenges. Free datasets, notebooks, and a large learning community.
typicalTiming: Competitions open and close year-round on independent schedules.
eligibility: Open to anyone with a free Kaggle account; some prize competitions have eligibility rules.

title: WHO Internship Programme
description: Internships at WHO headquarters and regional/country offices, giving students exposure to global public health, health technologies, and policy work. Placements span technical and programmatic areas.
typicalTiming: Positions are posted on a rolling basis throughout the year via the WHO careers portal.
eligibility: Students enrolled in a degree programme or recent graduates, meeting WHO's education and language requirements.

title: Chevening Scholarships
description: Fully funded one-year master's scholarships in the United Kingdom for outstanding future leaders from around the world, including students in engineering, science, and health disciplines.
typicalTiming: Applications typically open in the summer and close in the autumn for the following academic year.
eligibility: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries with a bachelor's degree, work experience, and an offer for an eligible UK master's.

title: DAAD Scholarships (Graduate Study in Germany)
description: A broad database of scholarships funding master's, doctoral, and research stays in Germany for international students, including many in biomedical engineering and life sciences.
typicalTiming: Deadlines vary by scholarship; search the official database for current programmes.
eligibility: International students and researchers; requirements differ by programme and are listed per scholarship.

title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA)
description: EU-funded fellowships and doctoral networks supporting researcher mobility and training across borders and sectors, widely used in biomedical, health, and engineering research.
typicalTiming: Calls follow the Horizon Europe work programme; postdoctoral fellowship calls are usually annual.
eligibility: Doctoral candidates and postdoctoral researchers; specific mobility and experience rules apply per action.

title: ASHG Annual Meeting
description: The world's largest human genetics and genomics meeting, featuring cutting-edge research, trainee programming, and networking. Offers reduced trainee registration and abstract presentation opportunities.
typicalTiming: Held annually in the autumn (October/November); abstract submissions open earlier in the year.
eligibility: Open to researchers, clinicians, and students worldwide; trainee membership provides discounts.

title: MICCAI Conference
organization: Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention Society (MICCAI)
description: The premier international conference for medical image analysis, computer-assisted intervention, and related machine learning. Features papers, tutorials, challenges, and a young scientist community.
typicalTiming: Held annually (usually autumn); paper submission deadlines are typically in the spring.
eligibility: Open to researchers and students worldwide; student registration rates and challenges available.

title: Wellcome Early-Career Awards
description: Funding for early-career researchers to develop their research identity and independent projects in areas relevant to human life, health, and wellbeing, including biomedical science.
typicalTiming: Application rounds run periodically each year; check the scheme page for current windows.
eligibility: Early-career researchers based at an eligible organization; residence and career-stage criteria apply.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)
description: Government-funded scholarships for international students to pursue undergraduate, master's, and doctoral study or research at Chinese universities, including biomedical engineering and life sciences programmes.
typicalTiming: Applications generally open in winter/early spring for autumn enrollment.
eligibility: International students meeting age and academic requirements; apply via universities or diplomatic missions.

title: MEXT Japanese Government Scholarship
organization: Japan Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
description: Japanese government scholarships supporting international students in undergraduate, graduate, and research programmes at Japanese universities, including engineering and biomedical fields.
typicalTiming: Embassy recommendation applications typically open in spring; university recommendation timing varies.
eligibility: International students meeting nationality, age, and academic criteria; apply via Japanese embassies or universities.

title: Amgen Scholars Program
description: A summer undergraduate research program hosted at leading universities across the US, Europe, and Asia, giving students hands-on laboratory experience in science and biotechnology plus a symposium.
typicalTiming: Applications generally open in winter for the following summer program.
eligibility: Undergraduate students; specific citizenship/enrollment criteria depend on the host region (US, Europe, Japan, etc.).

title: LinkedIn Jobs
description: A global professional network and job board where biomedical engineering and healthcare technology roles are posted by employers worldwide. Useful for internships, entry-level roles, and networking with recruiters.
typicalTiming: Roles are posted continuously; set alerts for new biomedical postings.
eligibility: Open to all with a free account; individual roles list their own requirements.

title: EURES European Job Mobility Portal
description: The official European job mobility portal listing vacancies across EU/EEA countries, including engineering and healthcare technology roles, with guidance on working and living in Europe.
typicalTiming: Vacancies are posted continuously by employers and public employment services.
eligibility: Primarily for jobseekers eligible to work in the EU/EEA; requirements vary per vacancy.

title: Coursera Courses & Specializations
description: An online learning platform offering university- and industry-led courses, specializations, and certificates in bioinformatics, medical imaging, AI in healthcare, and biomedical engineering fundamentals.
typicalTiming: Self-paced and scheduled cohorts available year-round.
eligibility: Open to anyone; financial aid and audit options available for many courses.

title: edX Courses & MicroMasters
description: A global online learning platform with courses and MicroMasters programs from universities in areas such as biomedical imaging, computational biology, and medical device innovation.
typicalTiming: Courses run self-paced and on scheduled sessions throughout the year.
eligibility: Open to all learners; audit options are free for many courses.

title: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship
description: A competitive summer research internship placing undergraduate students from partner countries in Canadian university labs across disciplines, including biomedical and health research.
typicalTiming: Applications typically open in summer/autumn for the following summer internship.
eligibility: Senior undergraduates from eligible partner countries; check current partner list and criteria.

title: IEEE EMBS Student Membership & Mentoring
organization: IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
description: Student membership in IEEE EMBS provides access to mentoring, technical communities, distinguished lectures, publications, and networking with biomedical engineering professionals worldwide.
typicalTiming: Membership can be joined year-round; mentoring and events run throughout the year.
eligibility: Students enrolled in relevant programmes worldwide; discounted student membership rates.

title: CERN openlab Summer Student Programme
description: A summer programme where students work on advanced computing projects, including machine learning and data science applications with relevance to medical imaging and healthcare technologies.
typicalTiming: Applications typically open in winter for the following summer.
eligibility: Undergraduate and master's students in computing, physics, engineering, or related fields.
